chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suheib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: When a man says to another man, "O passive sodomist!" and "O one copulated with in his backside!", then upon him is the Penalty (Hadd), the Penalty of the slanderer.'

key_terms.الْحَدّ: The fixed penalty prescribed by Sharia
key_terms.الْقَاذِف: The slanderer; one who commits Qadhf
key_terms.مَعْفُوج: Passive sodomist; one who is penetrated
key_terms.مَنْكُوح: Copulated with; one who receives intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the Hadd penalty for calling someone Ma'fuj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies that the terms 'Ma'fuj' and 'Mankuh fi duburihi' constitute formal slander (Qadhf) rather than mere insult, thereby triggering the standard Hadd penalty of 80 lashes. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the legal gravity of these specific sexual descriptors, linking them directly to the Quranic category of Qadhf which requires four witnesses for full proof. The narration highlights the precision of Imami legal interpretation in categorizing verbal abuse within the framework of public moral accountability.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, (the narrator says), ‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Aliasws was saying: ‘When the man says to the man, ‘O passive sodomist!’, and ‘O one copulated with in his backside!’, so upon him is the Penalty (Hadd), a Penalty (Hadd) of the slanderer’.
